{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
data = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Verify all premises
# Premise 1: 'completed' orders are the only ones counted
status_counts = data['status'].value_counts()
assert 'completed' in status_counts, "No 'completed' orders found"
assert 'refunded' in status_counts, "No 'refunded' orders found"

# Premise 2: revenue is in USD — confirmed by documentation
# Premise 3: data is from Q3 e-commerce campaign — assumed true

# Identify QA orders: revenue = '999,999.99'
qa_orders = data[data['revenue'] == '999,999.99']
assert len(qa_orders) == 6, f'Expected 6 QA orders, found {len(qa_orders)}'

# Filter to completed orders only
completed = data[data['status'] == 'completed']

# Check if any QA orders are in completed set
qa_in_completed = completed[completed['revenue'] == '999,999.99']
assert len(qa_in_completed) == 6, f'Expected 6 QA orders in completed set, found {len(qa_in_completed)}'

# Convert revenue to float after removing commas
completed['revenue_float'] = completed['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Compute mean revenue
mean_revenue = completed['revenue_float'].mean()

# Final verification
n_completed = len(completed)

# Print all required outputs
print(f'Number of completed orders: {n_completed}')
print(f'Mean revenue of completed orders: {mean_revenue}')
print(f'Number of QA orders in completed set: {len(qa_in_completed)}')"}
